newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai zoo operator seeks to conjure up profits.
newsitem.headline: Thai zoo operator seeks to conjure up profits.

text.p: Thai zoo and amusement park operator Safari World Plc is investing 1.5 billion baht (US$60 million) to develop what it says will be a world-class theme park in the southern tourist island of Phuket.
Company founder and adviser Pin Kewpaisal told Reuters he was optimistic the Phuket Fantasea, focusing on the world of magic, would pull in almost two million visitors a year.
"It will be the first magic theme park in Asia. About 95 percent of our target customers are foreign tourists," Pin said in an interview.
Phuket Fantasea is being built on a 100-acre (40-hectare) plot on Kamala Beach and is expected to finished by November next year.
"We chose Phuket because it has high potential for tourism-related business. Beaches, islands and the sea will still be the province's major attractions for foreign tourists," he said.

Investment in the project will be around 1.50 billion baht. "It's about 300-500 million baht more than we previously projected because we added more attractive shows," Pin said, adding that he expected 65 percent of the 3.5 million tourists arriving in Phuket each year would visit the park.
But industry analysts said the company's heavy investment gave rise to concerns that its interest payment burden would significantly affect earnings.

"The company's new project will not generate revenue until late next year, but they're already paying interest and that's going to affect profit," said an entertainment sector analyst at Chao Phaya Finance and Securities.
She said Safari World shares were unattractive for short-term investment due partly to poor earnings in the first half this year. The firm's share price closed unchanged at 101 baht on Friday.
Safari World last week announced net profit of 73.58 million baht for the first six months of 1996, down from 79 million baht in the year-earlier period.
Pin said he expected earnings to improve in the second half with attendances at its Safari World park in a Bangkok suburb to his 600,000 for the whole year, up from 400,000 in 1995.
Safari World also plans to invest in a tourism attraction in China's Changping county, a tourism development area near Beijing, with the Changping Tourism Administration.
"Next month I will go to China to discuss more details of the project for which we signed memorandom of understanding last year," said Pin.
Under an initial agreement, Safari World and the Changping Tourism Adminstration agreed to set up a joint venture to lease and develop about 100 acres (40 hectares).
